originality.rationale: The theorem is for all even-cardinality cyclic vertex intervals on even cycles. The closest inspected complete published-finding corpus theorem counts nonempty centered graph balls, which in even order have odd-size proper arcs; its all-radius family shatters every triple, unlike the n prohibited triples here. The inspected all-geodesics result permits a triple in even order only when it contains antipodes, and has a different mixed-dimensional homotopy type. A 2022 primary source proves sample compression for cycle balls, not the even-interval exact support or integral topology. The earlier unrestricted interval result proves a VC bound and an online recurrence, but not this parity-filtered theorem. The odd-order analogue is explicitly omitted because ball complementation covers its shattering counts. Exact published-finding corpus and own-ledger queries were checked; unindexed historical equivalences remain a risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unpublished equivalences in cyclic-range-space topology may exist; no claim of exhaustive historical priority.

value.rationale: The exact all-order parity-filtered shattering complex is a motivated refinement of a canonical cyclic geometric range class. It identifies precisely n missing triangular faces, proves those holes do not create fundamental-group obstructions, and classifies the integral homotopy as a wedge of exactly C(n-1,3)-n 2-spheres, including the small exceptional boundary n=4. This is structural topological information not implied by the previously known VC dimension three or radius-restricted graph-ball count; the exclusion of odd cycles handles a genuine known-coverage boundary.
